thread:
Tara (PM): quick sync — we need to decide prioritization for the next model catalog wave. constraints: bench time, pin policy, and a clear deprecation path for older variants
Derek (Eng): +1. scope question: do we treat slimline models (quantized, 4-bit) the same as full FP16 for onboarding?
Leila (ML): they should have different acceptance gates. bench metrics for slimline need tolerances on P50/P90 and hallucination delta vs baseline
Sam (Ops): ops-wise, slimline -> smaller infra bump. but routing/fallback complexity increases if we mix variants per customer
Zoe (CS): customers asked for guaranteed pin windows. they expect a 6mo grace period when we pin a model and 90d notice for deprecations
Tara (PM): proposal: two-tier onboarding lane — "fast-onboard (slim)" and "full-onboard (baseline)". fast-onboard gets lighter bench (latency/cost) + curated sample eval. full requires full eval battery and regression tests
Derek (Eng): rollout plan? canary first? what's rollback criteria?
Tara (PM): canary lanes required for full-onboard. fast-onboard can go straight to cohort canaries only (smaller blast radius). rollback if quality regression > 3% on our golden prompts or latency P90 > SLO
Leila (ML): suggested bench pass conditions (fast-onboard): P50 < 120ms, token-cost delta < 15% vs baseline, test-suite pass rate >= 92% for core intents
Leila (ML): full-onboard: P50 < 100ms, P90 < 400ms, hallucination delta < 1.5% absolute, eval pass >= 97%
Sam (Ops): operational asks: pin TTL should be explicit in onboarding artifact. also we need an "auto-fallback" policy config per model: prefer pin -> fall back to compatible variant -> fallback to hosted small. can we standardize config?
Derek (Eng): yes. define a JSON config on model object: {
  "pin_ttl_days": 180,
  "canary_cohort_pct": 5,
  "fallback_policy": ["variant-compat","regional-hosted"]
}
Derek (Eng): (inline) we'll add schema in the catalog service and expose via API
Zoe (CS): for enterprise customers who pay for pins, we need SLA language: guaranteed pin duration plus an opt-in extension (+paid)
Tara (PM): decision items for this thread:
- Approve two-tier onboarding lanes (fast vs full)
- Bench pass thresholds for each lane (Leila to finalize)
- Default pin TTL = 180 days, opt-in extensions allowed (sales/CS)
- Canary and rollback criteria (Eng/Ops to codify)
- Deprecation notice windows: 90d notice + migration credits for pinned customers
Sam (Ops): deprecation flow: 90d notice -> recommended migration variant + migration playbook -> 30d soft-landing (redirect traffic to fallback if not moved) -> final retire. we should track customers with pins separately in the console
Leila (ML): also add an automated drift check after 30d of production traffic. if drift > threshold, trigger quick-eval and rollback or hotfix path
Derek (Eng): implementation plan: week 1 schema + API, week 2 catalog UI flags + rollout-bot integration, week 3 canary orchestration and auto-fallback wiring
rollout-bot: scheduled: integration-tests -> green in CI; deploying canary lanes to staging 1777777400
Zoe (CS): can we commit to communication templates for customers? I can draft 90d/30d/7d notices and migration playbook snippets
Tara (PM): yes please. next steps owners: Leila finalize thresholds by EOD Thu, Derek + Sam to draft schema & rollback playbook by Mon, Zoe to draft comms by Tue. I'll collate and pull into a short PRD
Derek (Eng): noted. any objections to default pin TTL=180d?
Zoe (CS): fine from CS POV as long as paid extensions exist
Sam (Ops): fine, but ask: what about emergency security deprecations? TTL should allow immediate revocation for CVEs
Tara (PM): agreed — emergency revocation clause stays. add to PRD
Leila (ML): I'll add concrete test cases + toy eval set for fast-onboard to speed bench runs
Tara (PM): great. tagging here @Derek (Eng) @Leila (ML) @Sam (Ops) @Zoe (CS) — if no objections by EOD we'll spin up the PRD and kickoff. :thumbsup:
Derek (Eng): :thumbsup:
Sam (Ops): :shipit:
Zoe (CS): 👍
Leila (ML): ack
Tara (PM): thanks team — closing this thread when PRD draft links up.
